claims.object_text: regulates synaptic plasticity through AMPA receptor trafficking
claims.quote: Synaptic Ras GTPase-activating protein 1 (SYNGAP1) regulates synaptic plasticity through AMPA receptor trafficking.
SYNGAP1 mutations have been found in human patients with intellectual disability (ID) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

Almost every individual with SYNGAP1-related ID develops epilepsy, and approximately 50% have ASD.

Male mice with a heterozygous mutation in the Syngap1 gene (Syngap1-/+ mice) created by Seth Grant's group
Syngap1-/+ mice showed increased locomotor activity, decreased prepulse inhibition, and impaired working and reference spatial memory, consistent with preceding studies.
